text:
sophie: Quick heads-up — we’re kicking off a lightweight adapter compatibility run tomorrow for Snowflake -> Redwood ingest -> vector DBs (qdrant/pinecone). Main objective: find edge-case failures before the marketplace bundle.

kevin: +1. scope? schema changes, large VARIANTs, schema-on-read quirks?

sophie: Exactly. Focus on: nested VARIANT arrays, NULL-heavy columns, timestamp/timezone drift, very wide rows (>1MB payload), and streaming CDC ordering. Also test Delta Share and Databricks autoloader flows.

maria: I can own Snowflake test harness. Will create 6 synthetic datasets (small/med/large + nested + nullable). ETA EOD tomorrow. @kevin can you add the Databricks side?

kevin: Yep — will spin up a small cluster and run autoloader snapshots + streaming microbatches. I’ll also validate schema evolution scenarios (add/drop column, renamed fields).

raj: I’ll run vectors ingest to qdrant and pinecone with our current adapter. Will watch for ID collisions and metadata truncation. Also will test hybrid embeddings (sparse + dense).

alex: Heads-up on resource limits: qdrant test index with 1M vectors will blow the free tier. I’ll use a trimmed load (100k) but with pathological payloads to replicate truncation.

integration-bot: Reminder: create run tickets in #eng-platform-runbooks with label "adapter-compat-2153". Use template: runbook.redwood/adapter-compat-template

maria: putting the datasets and SQL in a shared folder: <https://go.redwood/sf-adapter-tests|Snowflake test data> — contains sample VARIANT rows and JSON arrays.

sophie: Acceptance criteria proposal:
- No 5xx from connector during ingestion
- Schema drift handled without data loss for add/drop/rename (can tolerate tombstoned fields)
- Metadata preserved up to 4KB per vector (truncate only with explicit warning)
- Timezone sanity: roundtrip timestamps match source within 1s for streaming tests

olivia: I can add alerting hooks in Console so we capture token/cost deltas during the run. Send me expected queries per dataset.

raj: Quick config snippet for qdrant adapter I’ll use:```yaml
adapter: qdrant
batch_size: 512
metadata_limit_bytes: 4096
retry_policy:
  max_retries: 5
  backoff: exponential
```

kevin: For Databricks autoloader, I’ll run:```scala
val df = spark.readStream.format("cloudFiles")
  .option("cloudFiles.format", "parquet")
  .load("s3://sf-test-bucket/exports/")
```
and then write to our staging topic.

darren: Who’s owner for the post-run triage? Need a single thread to consolidate failures and root-cause tags.

sophie: I’ll own triage and summary. Plan: run tomorrow 10am PT, 3h window, quick triage at 2pm PT and formal findings doc by Friday.

maria: added test matrix and checklist to the shared folder. Link in the run ticket.

kevin: I’ll post logs and minimal repro snippets directly to the ticket.

olivia: I’ll wire alerts to #partnerships and create a temporary dashboard for token/cost per run.

raj: If we hit a metadata truncation case, I’ll create a small repro (1 row) and attach to ticket.

integration-bot: Ticket created: RUN-2153-adapter-compat. Assigned: maria, kevin, raj, sophie.

sophie: Perfect. If anyone finds a blocker earlier, ping me @sophie or drop in #partnerships — would rather catch issues pre-run. :eyes:
